newsitem.title: USA: Florida ruling means case to go to trial in June.
newsitem.headline: Florida ruling means case to go to trial in June.

text.p: A Florida judge on Friday ordered a lawsuit against the tobacco industry, which includes claims under the state's anti-racketeering laws, to go to trial during the week of June 30, 1997.
Palm Beach County Circuit Judge Harold Cohen denied a motion by tobacco companies to stop the state of Florida from suing the industry under the state's so-called RICO laws.

The claims under state Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organization law were added last month to Florida's existing lawsuit, which seeks at least $1 billion in compensation for treating smoking-related illnesses.
Florida had said that a victory using RICO would let the court triple the damages claimed by the state.
Cohen ruled that the state had the right to add RICO counts to the case but said that the state would be held to a criminal standard in proving its case.
"The state has alleged and will be required to prove criminal intent by the defendants," he said.
